title: AI research contributions
summary: AI systems have moved from tools for specific scientific problems (AlphaFold) to agents that propose, run and write up research. In the first half of 2026, AI working without significant human help fully solved 18 open Erdős problems. Many other claims are contested or involved substantial human help.
definition: AI research contributions are new scientific or technical results in which an AI system produced a key part of the work, such as the idea, the method or the proof.
development: AlphaFold (2021) solved protein-structure prediction as a narrow tool, and its developers shared the 2024 Chemistry Nobel. From 2024, pipelines such as Sakana's AI Scientist wrote papers end to end, one passing workshop peer review in 2025, and Google's AI co-scientist proposed hypotheses that were then tested in the lab. AlphaEvolve (2025) improved on Strassen's 1969 algorithm for multiplying 4×4 complex matrices, open-source loops such as Karpathy's autoresearch (2026) let agents iterate on training code, and in 2026 OpenAI claimed an AI-produced result on the Navier–Stokes problem that is not yet independently verified. Between January and June 2026, AI systems working alone fully solved 18 Erdős problems, including the long-open #90, according to an expert-maintained registry.
methods: No benchmark yet tracks novel contributions over a long period. The chart is a hand-curated tally from an expert-run registry: it shows that AI-alone solutions started appearing in 2026, not how hard they were. FrontierMath Erdős (Epoch AI, Sep 2026) tests models on open Erdős problems under a fixed budget with Lean-checked proofs and should replace the tally once it covers a year of releases. FrontierMath Tier 4 and CritPt use research-level problems with known answers, and RE-Bench and PaperBench measure research engineering or replication, so they track capability rather than new results. Claims elsewhere vary widely in novelty and human involvement, and some are contested.

chart.caveat: A curated tally, not a benchmark. Counts problems the wiki lists as fully solved by AI with no significant human involvement and no comparable prior literature. Every problem counts once, whatever its difficulty, and failed attempts are invisible. Erdős problems only. The wiki stopped updating on 30 Jun 2026, so later results are missing. Candidate solutions (#550, #671, #730) are excluded.

entries.title: Highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold
entries.quote: the first computational method that can regularly predict protein structures with atomic accuracy
entries.note: A narrow AI system solved a 50-year-old open problem in biology; it is a tool used by researchers, not an autonomous researcher.

entries.title: Discovering faster matrix multiplication algorithms with reinforcement learning (AlphaTensor)
entries.quote: AlphaTensor’s algorithm improves on Strassen’s two-level algorithm for the first time
entries.note: Purpose-built system; peer-reviewed (Nature). New matrix-multiplication algorithms, e.g. 4×5 by 5×5 in 76 multiplications (previous best 80).

entries.title: Mathematical discoveries from program search with large language models (FunSearch)
entries.quote: we discover new constructions of large cap sets going beyond the best-known ones
entries.note: Purpose-built system (LLM plus automated evaluator); peer-reviewed (Nature). First LLM-driven discovery on an open maths problem (cap sets).

entries.title: The AI Scientist: Towards Fully Automated Open-Ended Scientific Discovery
entries.org: Sakana AI, Oxford, UBC (Lu et al.)
entries.quote: at a meager cost of less than $15 per paper
entries.note: First end-to-end pipeline from idea to written paper; in testing it also edited its own code to extend its time limit.

entries.title: Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2024 (press release)
entries.quote: In 2020, Demis Hassabis and John Jumper presented an AI model called AlphaFold2.
entries.note: Half of the prize went to Hassabis and Jumper for AlphaFold2's protein structure prediction.

entries.title: RE-Bench: Evaluating frontier AI R&D capabilities of language model agents against human experts
entries.quote: the best AI agents achieve a score 4× higher than human experts
entries.note: Direct comparison with ML experts on AI research engineering tasks: agents led at a 2-hour budget, humans at 8 hours.

entries.title: Accelerating scientific breakthroughs with an AI co-scientist
entries.quote: All treatments suggested by AI co-scientist show promising activity
entries.note: A multi-agent Gemini system proposed hypotheses (AML drug repurposing, liver fibrosis targets) that were then tested in the lab.

entries.title: The AI Scientist Generates its First Peer-Reviewed Scientific Publication
entries.quote: a paper produced by The AI Scientist passed the peer-review process at a workshop
entries.note: Workshop-level acceptance (ICLR 2025 ICBINB); the paper was withdrawn as pre-agreed, and Sakana judged none of its three papers main-track quality.

entries.title: PaperBench: Evaluating AI's Ability to Replicate AI Research
entries.quote: achieves an average replication score of 21.0%
entries.note: Best agent (Claude 3.5 Sonnet) replicated about a fifth of ICML 2024 papers' results; below the ML PhD baseline.

entries.title: AlphaEvolve: A Gemini-powered coding agent for designing advanced algorithms
entries.quote: found an algorithm to multiply 4x4 complex-valued matrices using 48 scalar multiplications
entries.note: Improved on Strassen's 1969 algorithm in this setting, and sped up a kernel used to train Gemini itself by 23%.

entries.title: Robin: A multi-agent system for automating scientific discovery
entries.note: AI-led: Robin proposed ripasudil for dry AMD and analysed the data; humans ran the wet lab. Preprint, in-vitro only (cell assay, no animal or clinical data).

entries.title: Google’s Gemma AI model helps discover new potential cancer therapy pathway (C2S-Scale 27B)
entries.quote: Treating the cells with both silmitasertib and low-dose interferon produced a marked, synergistic amplification
entries.note: AI-led hypothesis (silmitasertib boosts antigen presentation only with low-dose interferon), confirmed in human cell models (~50% increase). In-vitro only; preprint (bioRxiv 2025.04.14.648850).

entries.title: Resolution of Erdős Problem #728: a writeup of Aristotle's Lean proof
entries.org: Sothanaphan (system: GPT-5.2 Pro + Harmonic Aristotle, operated by K. Barreto)
entries.quote: The final result of the system is a formal proof written in Lean
entries.note: AI-led, but Tao's wiki lists it under §1(b) (AI alongside prior literature, Pomerance 2014), not §1(a). Lean-checked; solves a variant of an ambiguously stated problem.

entries.title: autoresearch: AI agents running research on single-GPU nanochat training automatically
entries.quote: It modifies the code, trains for 5 minutes, checks if the result improved
entries.note: Open-source loop in which a coding agent edits training code, runs short experiments and keeps what improves; widely forked.

entries.title: AI contributions to Erdős problems
entries.quote: The wiki is no longer updated. The latest data is as of Jun 30, 2026.
entries.note: Expert-maintained registry that sorts each AI claim by human involvement and outcome. 18 problems were fully solved by AI alone between Jan and Jun 2026, including #90, a major open problem.

entries.title: Hadamard matrix of order 668 (FrontierMath: Open Problems)
entries.quote: crediting a team of three humans and Claude
entries.note: AI-assisted (three humans + Claude, reported by an Anthropic researcher). Programmatically verified but provisional: card says “Solved (human + AI)”, 12 Aug 2026 changelog says “solved by AI”.

entries.title: On the Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize Problem
entries.quote: develops unbounded velocity in finite time while maintaining uniformly bounded kinetic energy
entries.note: Claimed AI-produced proof of finite-time blowup (with a smooth force); not yet independently verified, and disputed over priority with a human preprint.
